inter_profile_sharing.label: Cross-zone sharing
inter_profile_sharing.effect: Installs Inter Profile Sharing in the affected profiles and grants android.permission.INTERACT_ACROSS_USERS. After that, files, links, and clipboard content can be passed between zones.
inter_profile_sharing.cost: Opens a deliberate channel through boundaries that are otherwise sealed - the same category as the Immich bridge before it. The channel is narrow and only triggered by you, but it exists. Without a sharing password set, the transfer is UNENCRYPTED over a local port, and the app itself warns that other apps in the same profile could then read along.
inter_profile_sharing.verified: Measured end-to-end on our own emulator build (emu64x, Android 17, 2026-09-15): text shared in user 0, arrived in user 10 as 'New shared text' with the correct content. The service listens on 127.0.0.1:2411. The adb grant survives app updates and restarts.
manual: Set the same sharing password in ALL involved profiles (Settings -> Security -> Sharing Password). Without an identical password, the profiles won't find each other.
Turn on encryption - without a password it can't be enabled and the transfer runs in plaintext.
Observe in Lab for 48h before use (our own rule for new third-party apps), especially because this app by construction carries data across zone boundaries.

private_space_vaults.label: Bitwarden in Home's Private Space
private_space_vaults.effect: Pure documentation decision, not scriptable - Private Space is set up via Settings.
private_space_vaults.cost: Three seconds per access. In exchange, the most valuable app isn't permanently decrypted in the most-used profile, but at rest. WARNING: an unlocked Private Space occupies one of the three runtime slots - keep it short, otherwise Cloud gets evicted.
manual: Settings -> Security and Privacy -> set up Private Space, assign its own lock.
Move Bitwarden there and lock it again after every use.
The clipboard is SHARED between the owner and Private Space - copying a password out lifts the boundary for that content.

work_profile.label: Work profile in Home instead of a secondary Cloud profile
work_profile.effect: Creates a managed profile under Home (profile owner: Shelter) and installs the apps intended for it there. Customer calls then show names from company contacts, even while you're in Home privately - looked up, not copied.
work_profile.cost: Play would run in the work container: the 'no Play in Home' rule then only applies to the personal area. A work profile isolates more weakly than a secondary user - it runs alongside and the framework deliberately opens channels (contacts, share menu, notifications). Acceptable for apps the company entrusts with all its data anyway, wrong for consumer apps.
work_profile.verified: Measured on the emulator (2026-09-15): managed profile can be created via pm/dpm, Shelter as ManagedProfileOwner(parentUserId=0), apps installable, own VPN slot alongside Tailscale in Home, and cross-profile contact resolution from Home (phone_lookup_enterprise -> hit, phone_lookup -> no hit). The AOSP dialer uses ENTERPRISE_CONTENT_FILTER_URI (incallui/CallerInfo.java:348).
work_profile.unverified: WHETHER INTUNE MAM WORKS INSIDE IT. Company Portal needs sandboxed Play, which doesn't exist for the x86_64 emulator target. Only verifiable on real hardware. As long as that's open, this feature remains a hypothesis.
manual: Install Shelter from F-Droid or Accrescent in Home BEFORE provisioning runs - without the app no profile owner can be set.
After creation: sign in to Intune in the Company Portal inside the work profile, then Outlook and Teams.
Check whether Conditional Access with 'require app protection policy' takes effect - that's the open question this feature hinges on.

microsoft_365.label: Microsoft 365 as the work profile's stack
microsoft_365.effect: Installs Teams, Outlook, Authenticator and the Intune Company Portal into the managed work profile. Company Portal is the MAM agent: the employer applies app protection policies through it, and Conditional Access can require them before mail or chat data is released.
microsoft_365.cost: An agent that answers to the employer runs on the device. It cannot see the personal profile - that is precisely what the zone model buys - but inside the work profile it enforces policy, can wipe, and decides whether apps start at all. It also makes sandboxed Play load-bearing in the work container: without Play, Company Portal does not run.
microsoft_365.unverified: Whether Intune MAM accepts a Shelter-owned profile is the open question of the whole work zone (see work_profile). Company Portal needs sandboxed Play, which the x86_64 emulator target does not have. Only real hardware can answer it.
manual: Sign in to Company Portal inside the work profile FIRST, then Outlook and Teams - the other two expect an enrolled profile.
Do not enable google_workspace at the same time: two MAM agents in one profile is not a configuration any employer intends.

google_workspace.label: Google Workspace as the work profile's stack
google_workspace.effect: The same zone, filled by the other vendor: Gmail, Drive and Calendar in the managed work profile, with Android Device Policy as the MAM agent. It exists so the work zone is demonstrably not a Microsoft special case - the architecture is 'a managed profile with an employer's agent in it', whoever that employer buys from.
google_workspace.cost: Same shape as microsoft_365, plus a Google account becomes load-bearing for the work zone: Device Policy, Gmail and Drive all expect Google services, so sandboxed Play is not optional there. A device whose personal side is deliberately Play-free then carries Play in the work container.
google_workspace.unverified: Nobody has run this. The package names are reasoned guesses (pkg_status: unverified) and no run has enrolled a profile through Device Policy. Treat it as the documented alternative, not as a tested path.
manual: Enroll the work profile through Android Device Policy first, then sign in to Gmail, Drive and Calendar.
Do not enable microsoft_365 at the same time.

eid_germany.label: German eID (AusweisApp) in Home
eid_germany.effect: Installs AusweisApp, the official eID client for the German ID card. It reads the card over NFC and authenticates against public-sector and bank services.
eid_germany.cost: Region-specific, and useless outside Germany. It is also the one entry in the catalog whose signer nobody else corroborates: privacyguides/verified-apps documents F-Droid's rebuild, not the binary from the vendor's own release that we install (apks/certs/PROVENANCE.tsv). AppVerifier at first install on the device is the remaining check - which matters more here than elsewhere, because this app talks to an identity document.
manual: Verify the APK with AppVerifier at first install - its pin rests on a single download.
The card PIN never goes through the shell; set it up in the app.
